title: The Flexbox Mindset 🧠
description: Understand the container‑item relationship and the two axes that control flex layout.

slides.title: Goodbye Floats, Hello Flex! 👋
slides.content:
# The Modern Way to Layout

Before Flexbox, we used floats, inline‑block, and table‑cell for layouts – often hacky and unpredictable. Flexbox (Flexible Box Layout) was designed to distribute space and align content in a **one‑dimensional** row or column.

Flexbox gives you:
- Vertical centring without tricks.
- Equal height columns automatically.
- Source‑order independence with `order`.
- Space distribution that adapts to content.

All major browsers support it fully.

slides.title: Containers and Items 📦
slides.content:
# The Two Roles Flexbox involves two types of elements: - **Flex container** – the parent element that has `display: flex;` (or `inline-flex`). - **Flex items** – the direct children of that container. Only direct children become flex items; nested grandchildren are not affected by the container's flex properties. ```html
Item 1
Item 2
```

quizData.question: If a `<div>` has `display: flex;`, its grandchild elements become flex items.
quizData.explanation: Only direct children are flex items. The grandchildren are part of the normal flow unless their own parent is also flex.

slides.title: The Two Axes: Main & Cross ➡️⬇️
slides.content:
# Direction Defines the Axes

Flexbox works along two axes:
- **Main axis** – the primary direction items are laid out (left to right by default).
- **Cross axis** – perpendicular to the main axis (top to bottom by default).

These change when you modify `flex-direction`. If you set `flex-direction: column;`, the main axis becomes vertical and cross axis horizontal.

Understanding axes is crucial because alignment properties (`justify-content`, `align-items`) refer to either main or cross.

slides.title: Inline Flex Containers 📝
slides.content:
# `display: inline-flex;`

Like `inline-block`, an inline flex container behaves as an inline element from the outside, but inside it's a flex container. Useful when you want a container to sit within a line of text while its children use flex layout.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Flexbox = One‑Dimensional

Flexbox excels at rows OR columns, not both simultaneously. For two‑dimensional layouts (rows and columns at once), use CSS Grid. We'll cover that next chapter.
